doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Looks-based disrespect and motherhood making her tougher
summary: She has faced bias about looks, not race or gender; having a child made her assertive and self-reliant.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Are there issues in the music business with any racial issues, gender issues, or generational issues?

Oh constantly but I’ve been lucky, I’ve never had to deal with anything. I’ve been fine. I’ve never dealt with — the disrespect that I’ve dealt with has been more about looks and that kind of shallow stuff like that. It’s never been anything about race or gender. It’s always been whether or not I’m pretty enough sometimes, and that at other times whether or not I’m too pretty. It’s been ridiculous.

Yeah, those are the problems that I’ve had. I’ve never really had problems with the music. The music is the easy part, the fun part. And luckily everybody’s off my case about the other stuff now because I just stopped having it. And I’ll tell you, having a baby makes you a lot tougher as a human being.

You know I’ve got a 2-year-old boy who, I mean he’s a little wild child, you know they are. And so when you’re a parent you learn strength and you learn to be able to speak your mind in a firm clear way and not take no for an answer, because that’s very important for a toddler, you know? So now, any problem I had with that in the past I don’t anymore, because I used to be quite the pushover. I mean anything anyone would
say to me I would just be like, “Well, okay,” whether I agreed with it or not. I’m not like that anymore boy. No way.
Well that’s a good — I guess a good reputation to get — that she knows her business.

I mean you’re in this business for long enough and you do learn if you have your eyes and your ears open. You’ve got to. At the end it’s just you. All the people around you that you work with will come and go. And it’s you. You need to know. You need to be responsible for yourself.
